questions.question: Which of these is a terminal operation in a stream pipeline?
questions.explanation: collect produces a result and closes the stream. filter, map and sorted are intermediate and return new streams.

questions.question: What does this print? System.out.println(Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4).filter(n -> n % 2 == 0).map(n -> n * 10).collect(Collectors.toList()));
questions.explanation: filter keeps 2 and 4, then map multiplies each by 10, giving [20, 40].

questions.question: What does this code print? Stream.of("a", "b").peek(System.out::print);
questions.explanation: peek is intermediate and there is no terminal operation, so the pipeline never runs and nothing is printed.

questions.question: Stream<String> s = dishes.stream(); long n = s.count(); List<String> l = s.collect(Collectors.toList()); What goes wrong?
options: count() returns an int, not a long
The second terminal call throws IllegalStateException
questions.explanation: A stream can be consumed once. After count() it is closed, so call dishes.stream() again for the second result.

questions.question: What does it mean that streams are lazy?
options: Intermediate operations run only when a terminal operation starts the pipeline
Streams always run on a background thread
Streams copy the source before processing
Each operation waits one second before running
questions.explanation: Calling filter or map just records a stage. Data flows only when a terminal operation such as collect or count is called.

questions.question: What does this print? System.out.println(Arrays.asList(3, 1, 2).stream().sorted().findFirst().get());
questions.explanation: sorted puts the numbers in order 1, 2, 3, and findFirst returns an Optional holding 1, which get() unwraps.

questions.question: What is the main difference between map and flatMap?
options: map gives one element per input; flatMap turns each input into a stream and merges them
questions.explanation: flatMap flattens nested data, for example a list of order lists into one stream of orders.

questions.question: On Java 11, why does List<Integer> r = prices.stream().toList(); fail?
options: Stream.toList() was added in Java 16, so the method does not exist on Java 11
A List cannot hold Integer values
questions.explanation: On Java 11, write collect(Collectors.toList()) instead. It works on every Java version since 8.

questions.question: What does this print? System.out.println(IntStream.rangeClosed(1, 4).sum());
questions.explanation: rangeClosed includes both ends, so it streams 1, 2, 3 and 4, and their sum is 10.

questions.question: Which intermediate operation is stateful, needing to see every element before passing any on?
questions.explanation: sorted cannot emit the smallest element until it has seen them all. filter, map and peek handle one element at a time.
